hermetic was born since none of the alternatives I researched served all my needs
I used emanote with a custom theme for some time, but I was missing creating empty pages with no files underneath by just linking to them.

At the time of researching quartz as an alternative, it wasn't a standalone executable. You rather cloned its repository and set up a node environment to work with it, which isn't something I wanted to do in each project I wanted a wiki in.
I am a logseq user, but it is not a good fit for running in-project. Having to switch between graphs in a single app didn't feel natural for a project wiki.
hermetic is a static site generator for project-specific wiki.
no config required, single binary that just works
opinionated, not many knobs to turn, intended to work for my use-case

Create a folder for storing project wiki, then run hermetic serve WIKI_PATH
you just ran the serve command
Open the reported URL in the wiki.
The wiki is open in edit mode . You can now interact with and change it. Press ? to show keyboard shortcuts .
The files are saved as you change the contents.
You can either use the edit mode for reading,
or render a read-only HTML version of the wiki using the build command with hermetic build WIKI_PATH.
The HTML version is a static website that can be hosted using most HTTP serves or hosting providers (e.g. GitHub Pages ).
AI-generated content is something not intended to live in the wiki.
From my experience, it is never read, let alone read in detail, and would only pollute the graph and references.
If hermetic is a preferred way for users to read the AI-generated content, then it should live separately from the human-written parts.
In both edit mode and read-only mode you can invoke a modal that shows keyboard shortcuts by pressing ? (not when a block is being edited).
I mostly write in Journal, creating pages on demand.
I often mention 2 pages in the same block, which forms a connection between them.
The relationship can then be seen on both pages' sites, along with all the references made to them.
Note this page does not contain any link to the page in the Related section.
Neither is this the case in the opposite direction.
They rather are both mentioned in the same block on the index page.
